description: Implement IoT backend infrastructure: device registry with ledger backing, telemetry normalizer with anomaly detection, webhook handler with HMAC validation and rate limiting, zone graph updater with deduplication, and SSE broadcaster for real-time events. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 (MCP integration) and FEAT-003 (UI).
steps: Create src/iot/deviceRegistry.ts with Device entity, DeviceRegistry class maintaining Map<deviceId, Device> backed by ledger events (iot.device.registered/deregistered). Zone validation against LEDGER_ZONES from src/types/events.ts. Methods: register(device), deregister(deviceId), get(deviceId), listByZone(zone), all(), private hydrateFromLedger(). Ledger events use zone='IOT', actor='system:iot-registry', deviceId, payload=device.

Create src/iot/telemetryNormalizer.ts with TelemetryNormalizer class. Input: vendor-specific payload (unknown). Output: NormalizedTelemetry { sensorValue: number, unit: string, anomaly: boolean, raw: unknown }. Constructor accepts optional thresholds per DeviceType. Default thresholds: RFID/barcode (0-100), GPS (-180 to 180), sensor (-50 to 150), camera (0-1). Anomaly flag set when value outside range.

Create src/iot/webhookHandler.ts with WebhookHandler class and Express middleware. Dependencies: DeviceRegistry, TelemetryNormalizer, BondedLedger, SSEBroadcaster, secret from process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET. Validates: deviceId exists, timestamp within 60s, HMAC-SHA256 signature. Rate limiter: 1000 req/min per deviceId using RateLimiter from src/middleware/rateLimit.ts with key 'device:<deviceId>'. On success: normalize → append LedgerEvent (zone='IOT', actor='device:<deviceId>', eventType='iot.telemetry.received', deviceId, payload=normalized) → broadcast via SSEBroadcaster. On failure: push to in-memory retry queue, retry 3x with exponential backoff (100ms, 200ms, 400ms).

Create src/iot/zoneGraphUpdater.ts with ZoneGraphUpdater class. Listens to telemetry events from webhook handler. Maintains Map<zoneId, ZoneState> where ZoneState = { latestTelemetry, updatedAt }. Deduplication: Map<key, timestamp> where key = deviceId+eventType+sensorValue, ignore duplicates within 5s. Conflict resolution: last-write-wins by timestamp. Methods: onTelemetry(deviceId, zone, telemetry), getZoneState(zoneId), private extractZoneContext(deviceId, zone), private isDuplicate(deviceId, eventType, value).

Create src/iot/sseBroadcaster.ts with SSEBroadcaster class extending EventEmitter. Maintains Map<zoneId, Set<Response>> for subscribers and Map<Response, NodeJS.Timeout> for heartbeat intervals. Methods: subscribe(zoneId, res) registers SSE client and starts 30s heartbeat interval, unsubscribe(zoneId, res) removes client and clears interval, broadcast(zoneId, event) fans out SSEEvent to all zone subscribers, private sendHeartbeat(res) sends SSE comment line, private cleanupStale() removes connections inactive for 30s. SSEEvent schema: { type, deviceId, zoneId, telemetry, timestamp, anomaly }.

Create unit tests in tests/iot.spec.ts covering: DeviceRegistry CRUD (register, deregister, get, listByZone, all), zone validation (rejects invalid zones), deviceId uniqueness (rejects duplicate ids), hydration from ledger (reconstructs registry from iot.device.* events). TelemetryNormalizer: normalization for each DeviceType, anomaly detection for out-of-range values, raw payload preservation. WebhookHandler: HMAC validation (valid/invalid signatures), timestamp validation (fresh/expired), rate limiting (under/over limit per deviceId), retry logic (3 attempts with backoff), ledger append on success. ZoneGraphUpdater: deduplication (duplicate within 5s ignored, after 5s accepted), conflict resolution (last-write-wins by timestamp). SSEBroadcaster: subscription (client added to zone channel), broadcast (event fanned to all zone subscribers), heartbeat (sent every 30s), cleanup (stale connections removed).
acceptance_criteria: DeviceRegistry: register/deregister emit ledger events with zone='IOT', actor='system:iot-registry', eventType='iot.device.registered'/'iot.device.deregistered', deviceId, payload=device
DeviceRegistry: zone validation rejects devices with zones not in LEDGER_ZONES
DeviceRegistry: deviceId uniqueness enforced (register throws on duplicate id)
TelemetryNormalizer: produces NormalizedTelemetry { sensorValue, unit, anomaly, raw } from arbitrary payload
TelemetryNormalizer: anomaly=true when value outside device type's min/max threshold
WebhookHandler: validates HMAC-SHA256 signature using process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET, rejects mismatches
WebhookHandler: validates timestamp within 60s of server time, rejects expired
WebhookHandler: rate limits at 1000 req/min per deviceId, returns 429 when exceeded
WebhookHandler: on success, appends LedgerEvent (zone='IOT', actor='device:<deviceId>', eventType='iot.telemetry.received', deviceId, payload=normalized) and broadcasts SSEEvent
WebhookHandler: on failure, queues for retry with exponential backoff (100ms, 200ms, 400ms), stops after 3 attempts
ZoneGraphUpdater: deduplicates telemetry within 5s window (key: deviceId+eventType+sensorValue)
ZoneGraphUpdater: resolves conflicts by last-write-wins based on timestamp
SSEBroadcaster: subscribe(zoneId, res) adds client to zone channel, starts 30s heartbeat
SSEBroadcaster: broadcast(zoneId, event) fans out to all subscribers of that zone
SSEBroadcaster: cleanupStale() removes connections inactive for 30s
verification: npm run typecheck (no TypeScript errors in src/iot/*.ts)
npm test -- iot.spec.ts (all DeviceRegistry, TelemetryNormalizer, WebhookHandler, ZoneGraphUpdater, SSEBroadcaster unit tests pass)
npm run build (compiles successfully, dist/iot/*.js generated)
findings: All IoT backend infrastructure implemented and tested successfully. 32 unit tests pass. All modules compiled to dist/iot/. Key implementation notes: (1) DeviceRegistry uses ledger events for persistence with hydration support. (2) TelemetryNormalizer supports all 5 device types with configurable thresholds. (3) WebhookHandler implements HMAC-SHA256 validation, rate limiting at 1000 req/min per deviceId, and 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff. (4) ZoneGraphUpdater implements 5s deduplication window and last-write-wins conflict resolution. (5) SSEBroadcaster manages per-zone channels with 30s heartbeat and stale connection cleanup. Ready for FEAT-002 (MCP integration) to expose these as MCP tools and resources.
